prompt: Stage 3-3. You deliberately loss-streaked stage 2 and are on a 6-loss streak at 62 HP with 58 gold, level 6. You hold two completed items and a pair of your 3-cost carry. Losses now cost 8–9 HP each. Which is the exit condition that should end the streak?

options.label: Exit at 3-5: the streak ends when losses cost more HP than the gold is worth, and 8–9 HP per loss at 62 HP is that point
Exit now: buy the shop carry for the 2-star, slam both items, level to 7, and win-streak from 3-3
Keep streaking to 4-1 for the maximum streak gold and roll at 8

explanation:
A planned loss streak has a defined exit: the moment you can convert the gold into a board that wins, you convert. You are there. The shop offers the third copy of your 3-cost carry, you hold two completed items for it and a 3-cost tank, and you are at 58 gold with the interest cap already reached. Buying the carry, slamming both items and leveling to 7 costs about 24 gold and leaves you above 30, still earning 3 interest, with a board that beats the stage-3 lobby. Every further loss from here is an 8–9 HP trade for 1 gold of streak income: a terrible rate once the streak gold is already capped.

Waiting to 3-5 is a compromise that throws away two rounds of win-streak gold and 17 HP for nothing extra. Streaking to 4-1 is the Emerald version of the plan: it treats the streak as the goal instead of the setup, and arrives at level 8 with 90 gold, 30 HP and a lobby that has already stabilised. Loss streaks are a stage-2 tool with a stage-3 exit.
principle: A loss streak ends the round you can buy a winning board, not when the HP runs out.
commonMistake: Setting the exit by HP instead of by the board. Waiting for a threshold means you exit late, when the gold buys less.
